newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan hold first talks in three years.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan hold first talks in three years.

text.p: Indian and Pakistani diplomats held two hours of talks on Friday, their first in three years, to try and reduce tension on the subcontinent.
Delegations led by Indian Foreign Secretary Salman Haidar and his Pakistani opposite number Shamshad Ahmad met in an apparently cordial atmosphere at Hyderabad House in New Delhi.
The two sides have agreed to maintain a virtual news blackout until Monday when the talks are due to end.

"We had formal discussions followed by informal discussions. We discussed all topics," Haidar told reporters after the session. "The atmosphere was very amicable and friendly and we are very hopeful something will emerge from it."

Ahmad, who had his arm around Haidar's shoulders as the two emerged from Hyderabad House, said: "We'll resume our work tomorrow and continue to have discussions on all subjects. We met in a cordial atmosphere ... very cordial and very meaningful and we are hopeful."
The arch-rivals were resuming a dialogue that collapsed in January 1994 over the disputed Himalayan territory of Kashmir.
For Pakistan, Kashmir remains the "core issue", but India is hoping for progress on trade and economic cooperation as a means of easing tension between South Asia's threshold nuclear powers.
"Our focus is on cooperation," Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said in an interview published in the latest issue of the English-language Frontline magazine.
He said India wanted good neighbourly ties with Pakistan based on their 1972 Shimla Agreement.

"Naturally, Indian sovereignty is not negotiable," he declared. "Unless both of us understand this, difficulties will continue. We have given them (Pakistan) several concessions, like travel, unilaterally. We plan to expand these further."
India last week eased visa restrictions on Pakistanis after Islamabad released 38 Indian children held along with scores of adult Indian fishermen caught in Pakistani territorial waters.
If the talks between the two countries' top diplomats go well, the Indian and Pakistani foreign ministers will meet after an April 7-9 Non-Aligned Movement conference in New Delhi.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif could then meet at a May 12-14 summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation in the Maldives.
Kashmiri separatists held a rally in Srinagar, summer capital of the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, on Friday to protest at their exclusion from the India-Pakistan talks.

A strike called by the umbrella All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference closed most shops in the city. Police said they had detained Shabir Ahmad Shah, a separatist leader, and five others during the march by 100 Hurriyat supporters.

"It is a historical tragedy that India and Pakistan did not involve the Kashmiris, the principal party, in the peace talks," said a statement by Hurriyat, which groups about 30 religious and political parties who want a plebiscite in Kashmir.

Hurriyat supporters had planned a similar protest outside the venue of the talks in New Delhi but police prevented the demonstration and arrested 13 of their leaders, including the organisation's chairman Mirwaiz Omar Farooq, witnesses said.
India's main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said New Delhi should take a tough line on Kashmir.

"India should make its stand clear on the basis of the unanimous resolution adopted by parliament that Pakistan-occupied Kashmir was legally part of India and Pakistan must vacate the illegally occupied Indian territory. This should be the core issue," said BJP vice-president Krishan Lal Sharma, according to the Press Trust of India news agency.
Tension between India and Pakistan worsened after Kashmiris began a revolt against Indian rule in 1990 in the two-thirds of the territory held by New Delhi. Pakistan controls the rest.
India and Pakistan have gone to war three times since independence from Britain in 1947, twice over Kashmir.
